events.title: Serbia's student movement challenges Vučić at snap election
events.summary: Thousands of students rallied in Belgrade at a final student-led event before a snap national election, as a protest movement tries to turn street pressure into votes against 12 years of Vučić rule. The result will shape Serbia's EU accession path and its alignment with Russia.

events.title: Ebola spreads from DR Congo to Nigeria and Kenya, WHO warns
events.summary: An Ebola outbreak that began in DR Congo has spread to Nigeria and Kenya, and the WHO calls it 'complex'. Officials say the Nigerian and Kenyan patients may have crossed paths at Uganda's airport, which raises the risk of further spread and puts airport screening and travel rules under pressure in several states.

events.title: Israel locks down West Bank, demolishes Hebron buildings after attack
events.summary: Israel imposed a sweeping closure on the occupied West Bank and began demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers were shot dead; roadblocks are disrupting schools and medical care. UN Secretary-General Guterres voiced alarm, and the curbs on Palestinian movement and the risk of further escalation could draw in neighbours such as Jordan.

links.why: A security crackdown just days before the 27 October vote puts West Bank security and the government's response at the centre of the closing campaign.

events.title: Rubio urges Cubans to partner with CIA for political change
events.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly called on Cubans seeking change to form a 'discrete partnership' with the CIA, telling them 'now is the time' to act. The open appeal for regime change sharpens US pressure on Havana and could affect sanctions policy and migration flows toward the United States.

links.why: Both reflect a US push to reshape Latin American governments it opposes, following the capture of Maduro and the US-backed interim rule in Venezuela.

events.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
events.summary: Ukraine said Starlink was still restricted after Trump said the limits had been lifted, then said on 24 October the connection was restored and 'now stable'. Satellite links underpin Ukrainian military communications, so US control over access gives Washington leverage over the war and over how much European partners must fill the gap.

links.why: Both show US leverage over Ukraine's wartime position, from intelligence sharing to satellite access, shaped by Washington's shifting attention and backing.
links.via: US support for Kyiv's war effort

events.title: UK PM Burnham seeks talks on EU freedom of movement return
events.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he wants an 'honest discussion' about returning to EU freedom of movement, and Angela Rayner has backed the call for a debate. It is so far only a call for talks, but any move would reshape UK-EU migration, labour flows and relations with member states such as France, Germany, Ireland and Poland.

events.title: Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months in exile
events.summary: Opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela after 10 months in exile, entering a country run by an interim government under US-backed rule. Her return reshapes the political transition and the US stance toward Caracas, with consequences for oil investment and migrant flows.

links.why: The main opposition leader's return changes the political risk around the interim government that is signing oil deals with US and European companies.

events.title: Algeria sends troops to Niger, first foreign deployment since 1973
events.summary: Algeria's president has ordered troops into neighbouring Niger, the first Algerian deployment abroad since 1973. The move shifts the security balance in the Sahel and could change the calculations of Mali, Libya and other neighbours over borders, migration and trade routes.
